'''Katada Shrine''' (堅田神社) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=branch shrine}} (sessha) of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. It Ranks 15th among the 27 sessha of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Edited by Ujiyamada City Office (1929): pp. 9-11</ref>

It is the shrine that initiated the production of sacred salt (御塩, goshio) offered to both the Inner and {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Outer Shrine (Ise)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11633343}} at {{ill|Futami-ga-ura, Mie|en|Futami-ga-ura|qid=Q11371796|lt=Futamiura}}, enshrining the local deity.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 77</ref>

considered one of the candidate sites (論社) for both the "Enomura Shrine" and "Ōkunidama-hime Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}.<ref name="tm"/> The view that identifies Katada Shrine as "Ōkunidama-hime Shrine" was expressed by Watari Nobunori and {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|ja|伴信友|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomonobu Ban|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q4346747}}, while Sonoda Moriyoshi speculated that "Ōkunidama-hime Shrine" might have been located west of Katada Shrine.<ref name="sk3">Edited by Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p. 253</ref> {{ill|Ujiyoda Shrine|ja|宇治山田神社}} is also considered a candidate site for "Ōkunidama-hime Shrine."<ref name="sk3"/>

The shrine grounds cover an area of approximately 2,516 square meters (2 tan, 5 se, 11 bu).<ref name="uy">Edited by Ujiyamada City Office (1929): p. 10</ref> The {{ill|Shintai|en|Shintai|qid=Q327532|lt=Shintai}} (sacred object) is a stone, and the {{ill|honden|ja|社殿}} (main hall) measures approximately 1.3 meters in length, 1.5 meters in width, and 2.0 meters in height.<ref>Fukuyama et al. (1975): p. 150</ref>

== Enshrined Deity ==

The {{ill|kami|ja|祭神}} enshrined is Samitsu-hime no Mikoto (佐見都日女命).<ref name="ic">Edited by Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p. 95</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 70</ref> She is considered a local deity.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> If Katada Shrine is regarded as the successor to the ancient "Ōkunidama-hime Shrine," Samitsu-hime no Mikoto would be the daughter of {{ill|Isetsuhiko|en|Isetsuhiko|qid=Q17193127|lt=Isetsuhiko}}, the great land deity of {{ill|Ise Province|en|Ise Province|qid=Q864166|lt=Ise Province}}.<ref name="tm"/> The name "Samitsu" refers to an old place name of the area.<ref name="tm"/>

== History ==

When {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} visited Futami during her journey through the provinces, Samitsu-hime no Mikoto, the local deity, presented her with hard salt (堅塩, katajio).<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> Yamatohime-no-mikoto was pleased and established Katada Shrine.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk"/> However, Samitsu-hime no Mikoto did not offer the salt willingly; instead, she silently presented it without answering Yamatohime-no-mikoto’s questions, as a form of resistance to giving up her cultivated land.<ref name="tm"/> This event marked the origin of sacred salt production at Futamiura for offerings to the Inner and Outer Shrines.<ref name="tm"/>

Although the shrine's rituals were interrupted for a time, Arakida Ujiyuki revived them in 1434 (Eikyō 6). When Futami became shrine territory again in 1670 (Kanbun 10), the {{ill|Edo shogunate|ja|Tokugawa shogunate}} ordered the local people to perform festivals and shrine rebuilding, which they did with great dedication.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.isekanko.jp/k-cycling/course05.html|title=Course 05 Futami Route – Visiting Shrines, Meoto Iwa, and Somin’s Forest in the Land of Purification and Salt|publisher=Ise City Tourism Association|accessdate=2014-06-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026232640/http://www.isekanko.jp/k-cycling/course05.html|archivedate=2013-10-26}}</ref>

The shrine was rebuilt in March 1921 (Taishō 10).<ref name="uy"/>

== Surroundings ==

Katada Shrine is located at the western foot of Mt. Otonashi, directly across from the Futami General Branch Office of Ise City Hall.<ref name="ic"/> Nearby is the Futami inn district, and passing through it leads to {{ill|Futami Okitama Shrine|en|Futami Okitama Shrine|qid=Q64969614|lt=Futami Okitama Shrine}} and {{ill|Meoto Iwa|en|Meoto Iwa|qid=Q333875|lt=Meoto Iwa}} (the "Wedded Rocks").<ref name="gk"/>

It’s about a 6-minute walk (approximately 400 meters) from {{ill|Futaminoura Station|en|Futaminoura Station|qid=Q117376|lt=Futaminoura Station}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line}} of {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central}}.<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.yokoyama-vc.jp/marugoto/walking60/13.pdf|title=Route 13: The Sacred Salt Road|publisher=Yokoyama Visitor Center|accessdate=2014-06-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140608131007/http://www.yokoyama-vc.jp/marugoto/walking60/13.pdf|archivedate=2014-06-08}}</ref> It is also right in front of the Futami General Branch Office bus stop. By car, it is about a 1-minute (1.2 km) drive from {{ill|Futami junction|ja|二見ジャンクション|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futami Junction|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10880410}} via National Route 42 after exiting the {{ill|Ise Futami Toba Line|ja|伊勢二見鳥羽有料道路|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Futami Toba Toll Road|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢二見鳥羽ライン|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11378935}}.
